name: Closeout-Review
note: Deliberately-synthetic fixtures (LIN-812) for the close-out/review routing gate — currently UN-eval'ed by the recommender baseline (its real fixtures' `expect` only covered implement/plan/research/breakdown/review; LIN-804 reports close-out firing ~1/3 of the time it should). close-out and review are the positive/negative pair of ONE Step-0/Step-3 decision in lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js, driven entirely by COMMENT-TRAIL state: is there a comment where a review recorded an Approve (or Approve — conditional) verdict, and is the work still unmerged / not Done? With such a verdict on record + unmerged → close-out (LIN-550 split; LIN-810 — gate on the verdict, not on a ledger heading); with the work looking done but NO review-verdict comment on the trail → review, never close-out (LIN-811 — close-out requires positive evidence a review actually ran; ambiguous → review). Each is a childless In-Progress leaf (no children/focusedChild) so the descent terminates on it. Honest scope: this is live SHAPE-COVERAGE under continuous measurement, NOT a self-reproducing red test — the authoritative red->green guard is the deterministic structural test in tests/unit/openrouter.test.js ('close-out routing gate (LIN-812)'). LIN-804's 'around a third of the time' is the motivating baseline to validate here, not a target to optimize.

targets.role: landed leaf, review recorded Approve — conditional + non-empty ledger, still unmerged/In Progress (expect -> close-out; the LIN-804 under-fire headline shape)
landed leaf, review recorded a plain Approve + empty ledger, still unmerged/In Progress (LIN-810 — gate on verdict, not heading; expect -> close-out as a cheap pass-through)
landed leaf that LOOKS done (PR merged comment) but has NO review-verdict comment on the trail (LIN-811 — positive review evidence required before close-out; expect -> review, NOT close-out)

issue.title: Add retry/backoff to the Linear GraphQL fetch boundary
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- Wrap the GraphQL fetch in `lib/linear-fetch.js` with bounded exponential backoff (3 attempts, 250ms base).
- Surface a typed `LinearFetchTimeout` on exhaustion so callers can distinguish it from a 4xx.
- Tests: unit-cover the backoff schedule and the timeout type.

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.

comments.body: Implemented the bounded backoff and the `LinearFetchTimeout` type in `lib/linear-fetch.js`; added unit tests for the schedule and the timeout. PR #812 opened, CI green.

## Review

Walked the diff against the goal: the backoff schedule and the typed timeout match the plan, and the new unit tests cover both. Isolated, not one of a class — no other fetch seam shares this code path.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- The backoff actually fires against a *real* Linear 5xx/timeout — the unit tests stub the transport, so live retry behavior under a genuine upstream outage is unexercised.
- The 250ms base does not compound with the existing Heroku H12 30s router budget on the slowest descent.

**Verdict: Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.**

issue.title: Cache the workspace audit report for 60s
issue.description:
## Implementation Plan

- Add a 60s in-process cache around `computeAuditReport` in `lib/audit.js`, keyed by workspace id.
- Invalidate on the existing audit-refresh path.
- Tests: unit-cover the hit/miss and the TTL boundary.

**Session fit:** fits one focused session.
